summary: Rebuild #3 of M2-S02 (access step: permission sets and permission set groups for Tier 1, Tier 2 and Billing), a §4 repair of a documented step whose step gate is approved, triggered by reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md run 5 finding F-60: a TestUserFactory user holding Case_Agent_Core + Case_Tier1, inserting a Case under System.runAs(agent), failed with 'Operation failed due to fields being inaccessible on Sobject Case ... fieldNames: Subject,Origin,AccountId,Priority,EntitlementId'. Added seven fieldPermissions blocks to Case_Agent_Core.permissionset-meta.xml (Case.AccountId, Case.ContactId, Case.Description, Case.Origin, Case.Priority, Case.Subject, Case.SuppliedEmail; readable=true/editable=true), grounded in the M1-S02 Case Support/Billing layouts' Edit-behavior fields, milestone F-09/F-10/F-11 (ContactId/Description/SuppliedEmail required on layout), and the F-60 fixture itself for AccountId (TestDataFactory.createCases sets AccountId on the Case the agent inserts). Deliberately excluded Case.EntitlementId (stamped by M4-S03's before-save Flow, per the plan's entitlement design and F-60's own fix note) and Case.Type/Case.Reason (neither field appears on either Case layout). Case_Tier1, Case_Tier2 and Case_Billing were not touched: F-60 states plainly that 'Case_Tier1 adds none', and no source names a standard Case field any of the three delta personas write differently. Reworded Case_Agent_Core's <description> (193 chars, under both the 255-char ERROR and 200-char INFO thresholds) to state the addition and the EntitlementId exclusion. The checker's second PSVP-FLS-01 WARN, on Case_Agent_Core's EmailMessage grant, is left standing and explained rather than guessed: the persona does reply to emails (the set's own description and decisions.md D-M2S02-01 both say so) but no layout, workbook row or decision in this build enumerates which standard EmailMessage fields a reply populates, and inventing them would repeat the exact failure mode F-60 is a case study of. All three cited checkers exit 0 (Case PSVP-FLS-01 cleared; EmailMessage PSVP-FLS-01 remains as a named, explained residual); check-outputs is ok; all 8 XML files parse; the manifest is unchanged and still consistent (no new component, only field grants inside an existing file).
confidence_rationale: The Case half of this repair is HIGH by the Step 10 table: every added element (Case.AccountId, Case.ContactId, Case.Description, Case.Origin, Case.Priority, Case.Subject, Case.SuppliedEmail) traces to the M1-S02 layouts, F-09/F-10/F-11, or the F-60 fixture itself; all three cited checkers exited 0 on the first repair pass; check-outputs is ok; nothing was written outside artefacts/M2-S02/. Held to MEDIUM overall because one row could not be answered from any source on file: which standard EmailMessage fields the persona populates when replying has no layout, workbook row or decision naming them, so that PSVP-FLS-01 WARN is left as a recorded ambiguity rather than resolved by invented field names -- exactly the kind of guess F-60 is a case study against.

process_observations.observation: The repair stayed inside the one file the finding named. Case_Tier1, Case_Tier2, Case_Billing and the three PermissionSetGroup files needed no edit: F-60 itself says 'Case_Tier1 adds none', and re-running the group-composition checker after the edit still shows Case_Agent_Core referenced by all three PSGs with no naming or membership drift.

skills/admin/permission-sets-vs-profiles shipped PSVP-FLS-01 (WARN) between the last M2-S02 rebuild and this one, so this repair had a mechanical check to build against rather than relying only on the prose gotcha -- the same checker also caught the EmailMessage gap this report leaves as a named residual, which is exactly the kind of second-order catch a library fix is supposed to produce.

F-60 reached the build at M5, five milestone verifications and two org dry runs after M2-S02 was first marked tested and documented -- the gap survived every declarative-only check because nothing exercised the permission sets as the persona until an Apex test ran runAs(agent). Any other access-model step in this build (M2-S01's integration permission set, M2-S03's base profiles) that has not had an as-persona DML test run against it carries the same unverified risk this one just proved out.

No artefact in this build (layout, workbook row, or decision) names which standard EmailMessage fields a Tier 1/2/Billing reply populates, even though Case_Agent_Core's own description and decisions.md D-M2S02-01 both say the persona drafts EmailMessage records. The PSVP-FLS-01 WARN on EmailMessage is left standing rather than closed by a guessed field list.
This step is back at built; its tested and documented run records (and the M2 milestone verdict) again predate the current file contents and need to be re-run before they are trustworthy.

process_observations.followup_reason: A Case Feed / email-compose layout or Path step would name the specific EmailMessage fields the persona populates on reply, closing the residual PSVP-FLS-01 WARN with grounded fields rather than leaving it open.
